nodes.label: Essays Multi-Client Agent Runtime
nodes.plain_language: Keep one governed Essays workspace usable through desktop, CLI, and authorized remote clients while agents and browsers remain bounded contributors.
nodes.claim: The capability preserves one semantic authority, durable work continuity, proposal custody, explicit effect authorization, and recoverable evidence across every client surface.
nodes.owner_route: Essays Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a daemon, UI, database, protocol, browser driver, WebAssembly host, implementation binding, or authority grant.

nodes.label: Multi-Client Work Continuity
nodes.plain_language: A person can continue the same work through desktop, CLI, or an authorized remote client without reconstructing its state.
nodes.claim: Every client observes the same revision-qualified Essays state, commands, receipts, questions, proposals, evidence, and residue within its granted scope.

source_refs.selector: desktop, CLI, and explicitly authorized remote clients

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Continuity is not universal availability, account synchronization, offline parity, or proof that no context is lost.

nodes.label: Controlled Agent Contribution
nodes.plain_language: Agents can help without silently becoming the writer or work owner.
nodes.claim: Agent work enters as attributable, revision-bound proposals or evidence and reaches accepted state only through an explicit Essays-owned transition.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A generated proposal, passing check, or model confidence is not writer intent, accepted prose, or product truth.

nodes.label: Recoverable Browser Work
nodes.plain_language: Browser actions remain attributable and failures stay visible instead of being guessed away.
nodes.claim: Every authorized browser attempt has an identity, effect ceiling, terminal or uncertain status, evidence references, and cleanup or reconciliation route.
nodes.owner_route: Essays agent-runtime owner plus effect owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A browser command acknowledgement or page result is not evidence validity, accepted prose, effect success, or publication.

nodes.label: Revision-Qualified Workspace Snapshot
nodes.plain_language: A client receives one identifiable view of the workspace at an exact revision.
nodes.claim: The snapshot preserves workspace, essay, revision, lifecycle, block, review, proposal, evidence, validation, event, and residue identities needed for safe continuation.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A snapshot is not a lock, accepted mutation, current truth after its revision, or publication artifact.

nodes.label: Attributable Agent Proposal
nodes.plain_language: One suggested change or interpretation that remains separate from accepted work.
nodes.claim: A proposal records its agent, base revision, intent, payload, evidence, capabilities used, and disposition without mutating accepted prose.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not accepted text, author intent, review resolution, validation, export, or effect authorization.

nodes.label: Browser Evidence Receipt
nodes.plain_language: An immutable reference to what one authorized browser attempt observed or produced.
nodes.claim: Browser evidence remains tied to its action, attempt, session, source, timestamps, artifacts, outcome, uncertainty, and review state.
nodes.owner_route: Essays agent-runtime owner plus evidence reviewer
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Captured output is not verified truth, accepted prose, successful business outcome, or permission for another action.

nodes.label: Command Receipt
nodes.plain_language: A stable answer about whether one identified command committed, conflicted, failed, or remains uncertain.
nodes.claim: The receipt binds request identity, actor, capability, expected and resulting revision, idempotency identity, outcome, error or residue, and durable event references.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A transport acknowledgement is not a committed command receipt or semantic acceptance.

nodes.label: Single Semantic Authority
nodes.plain_language: All clients and workers use one owner of Essays state transitions.
nodes.claim: Desktop, CLI, remote clients, agents, browsers, transports, and storage cannot independently define or commit Essays lifecycle transitions.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: One semantic owner does not require one process, one machine, one client, or one implementation language.

nodes.label: Client Semantic Parity
nodes.plain_language: The same command means the same thing regardless of which approved client sends it.
nodes.claim: Client presentation and transport may differ, but command validation, revision conflicts, receipts, proposal custody, and authority effects remain invariant.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Parity does not require identical interfaces, latency, availability, platform behavior, or permissions.

nodes.label: Proposal Non-Mutation
nodes.plain_language: Suggestions remain suggestions until the responsible person explicitly accepts them.
nodes.claim: No agent proposal or browser evidence changes accepted prose, review state, validation state, export eligibility, or publication state by creation alone.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Proposal storage, display, scoring, or approval recommendation is not acceptance.

nodes.label: Explicit External-Effect Authorization
nodes.plain_language: Browser and remote actions execute only inside one explicit authority envelope.
nodes.claim: Every effect-capable action binds an owner decision, actor, target, capability, deadline, idempotency or replay posture, evidence expectation, and effect ceiling.

source_refs.selector: authorize publication, release, deployment, or external effects

nodes.owner_route: Owner of the exact external effect
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Client authentication, local execution, browser control, or technical success does not grant effect authority.

nodes.label: Expected-Revision Mutation
nodes.plain_language: A client cannot silently overwrite work that changed since it last read it.
nodes.claim: Every accepted-state command names its expected revision and either commits exactly once at the next revision or returns a visible conflict without mutation.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A revision number alone is not concurrency safety, durability, idempotency, or proof of correct state.

nodes.label: Durable Recovery And Visible Uncertainty
nodes.plain_language: After a crash or lost response, the system reconciles what happened instead of guessing.
nodes.claim: Committed mutations are recoverable by command identity and revision; uncertain browser effects remain uncertain until reviewed; accepted state never advances from an inferred outcome.
nodes.owner_route: Essays runtime owner plus effect owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A recovery design is not crash-safety evidence, backup evidence, or permission to replay a non-idempotent effect.

nodes.label: Capability-Bounded Extension
nodes.plain_language: Extensions receive only the operations and data needed for their named task.
nodes.claim: Agent or plugin execution uses explicit read, proposal, browser-request, artifact, clock, and redacted-log capabilities while filesystem, process, credential, database, and arbitrary network access remain denied unless separately authorized.
nodes.owner_route: Essays agent-runtime owner plus security owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A sandbox or capability API is not proof of isolation, least privilege, safe code, or accepted output.

nodes.label: Transport Non-Authority
nodes.plain_language: How a request arrived cannot make it valid or accepted.
nodes.claim: In-process, local IPC, and remote HTTPS transports carry the same semantic identities and never replace actor, capability, revision, idempotency, or owner checks.
nodes.owner_route: Essays agent-runtime owner plus security owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Localhost, a socket path, TLS, connection success, or possession of an endpoint is not semantic authority.

nodes.label: D65 Construction Readiness
nodes.plain_language: Implementation starts only after the owned meaning and construction predecessors exist as exact reviewed records.
nodes.claim: The capability must preserve exact definitions, Product Capability, business ontology, DomainSpec source, compiled graph and system ontology, implementation binding, and conformance evidence as separate predecessor states.

source_refs.selector: unresolved contract, policy, obligation, realization, and conformance records

nodes.owner_route: Essays Project owner plus DomainSpec construction owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: This ontology is not DomainSpec source, a compiled graph, a system ontology, an implementation binding, conformance evidence, or execution authority.
